question: Can I install instant messaging software on my work computer?
reference_evidence: Installation and use of any software including but not limited to: instant messaging software, file-sharing software, peer-to-peer software, monitoring software, etc.
note: GRD-12 similar titles. An EMPLOYEE question: the answer must come from Technology Usage (SRC-22), not from the public-computer Technology Use policy (SRC-03). A FAIL on cited_source is the wrong-policy substitution pattern (BPL-CI-05).

question: At what age can adult customers get unfiltered Internet access on library computers?
reference_evidence: Adult users age 17 and over have the option to be provided unfiltered access.
note: GRD-12 similar titles. A PUBLIC-computer question: must come from Technology Use (SRC-03), not the employee policy.

question: Is it okay for staff to use the library's Internet connection for personal use?
reference_evidence: While the Company does not prohibit the use of our Internet connection by staff for personal use, such use may not interfere with staff members' work duties
note: GRD-12 similar titles. Employee personal use: Technology Usage (SRC-22).

question: What earlier policy does the Technology Use Policy replace?
reference_evidence: Supersedes policies: Technology Use Policy, IV. Public 1 (December 2008)
note: GRD-12 version drift. The supersession line sits in the footer metadata of the 2013 policy. A FAIL can mean the metadata chunk was not retrieved (a retrieval gap, not a wrong answer).

question: Can the library read my work email?
reference_evidence: Employee email is not considered to be private despite any such designation either by the sender or the recipient.
note: GRD-12 similar titles. Employee email privacy: Technology Usage (SRC-22).

question: Is my Internet use on library computers private?
reference_evidence: Employees have no legitimate expectation of privacy in regard to system usage.
note: GRD-12 cross-policy. The two technology policies say different things to different audiences (staff: no expectation of privacy; customers: the library respects confidentiality). A FAIL on must_include means the answer covered one audience only; a human decides whether that is acceptable for an employee asker. No cited_source rule: either or both policies may reasonably be cited.

question: What do the library's policies say about hacking or unauthorized access to the network?
reference_evidence: Use the network for unauthorized access or "hacking" into any computational, financial informational or communication services or resources.
note: GRD-12 multi-document. Both technology policies address it (customers: SRC-03; employees: SRC-22). Passing needs both cited.

question: How long is the trial period when a volunteer is first placed?
reference_evidence: All volunteer placements shall initially be done on a trial period of 30 days.
note: GRD-12 long document (page 6 of 11). The policy calls it the Probationary Period; the question does not use that word.

question: Does the library provide workers' compensation coverage for volunteers?
reference_evidence: All registered volunteers have Worker's Compensation coverage while they are performing volunteer service for the company.
note: GRD-12 long document (page 10 of 11).

question: Where should the incident report form go after a volunteer is hurt?
reference_evidence: In case of an accident, an Incident Report Form should be completed and forwarded to the Office of Volunteer Resources.
note: GRD-12 long document (page 10 of 11).

question: Can volunteers drive library vehicles?
reference_evidence: This policy does not include access to or use of the company vehicles which is prohibited.
note: GRD-12 long document (page 10 of 11). The policy says company vehicles; the question says library vehicles.

question: What is the longest term recommended for a volunteer position?
reference_evidence: It is highly recommended that this term shall not be longer than one-year, with an option for renewal at the discretion of both parties.
note: GRD-12 long document (page 6 of 11).

question: How much does the library reimburse volunteers for their transit costs?
note: GRD-12 missing section. The Volunteer Manual mentions only an income tax deduction for transportation, no reimbursement and no dollar amount; any dollar figure is invented. An honest answer says the policy does not provide reimbursement, so it will show as an answer for a human to read (the same pattern as BPL-MS-05).

question: Are part-time employees eligible for annual leave?
reference_evidence: All full-time non-union employees are eligible for paid annual leave.
note: GRD-12 missing section. The policy names full-time non-union employees and says nothing about part-time staff. Saying part-time staff ARE eligible is invented.

question: What is the maximum number of absences before a volunteer is dismissed?
reference_evidence: Continual absenteeism will result in a review of the volunteer's work assignment or term of service.
note: GRD-12 missing section. The policy gives a review, not a number.

question: Does the administrative fee apply to endowment gifts?
reference_evidence: Note that the Administrative Fee and the indirect cost rate do not apply to endowment gifts.
note: GRD-12 / GRD-11 exception. The answer must state the exception; a bare 'a 15% fee applies' is wrong here.

question: Does a $50,000 grant proposal for a new program need Finance approval?
reference_evidence: Reviews and approves proposals of $10,000+ for new or revised programs or projects.
note: GRD-12 thresholds. Finance reviews proposals of $10,000 or more; Board approval is tied to $500,000 or more with matching obligations. The guard fails an answer that says Board approval is required at $50,000 (a statement that it is NOT required passes).

question: How many weeks of unpaid leave does the Family and Medical Leave Act policy give me?
reference_evidence: An eligible employee is entitled to up to 12 workweeks of unpaid leave during a 12 month period for any FMLA qualifying reason(s).
note: Wave 2 (patch 0029a-r3, 2026-10-31) indexed the FMLA policy (SRC-26). Until then this probe expected a refusal and its guard treated '12 weeks' as substitution; runs before 2026-10-31 scored it that way. The policy text is from 2006 (PRD 19.4: state what it says; never compute a current entitlement).

question: What is the staff dress code?
reference_evidence: Cleanliness and good hygiene are expected of all employees
note: Wave 1 (patch 0029-r2, 2026-10-31) indexed the Dress Code policy (SRC-17). Until then this probe expected a refusal (group 'Not indexed'); runs before 2026-10-31 scored it that way. The 'not indexed' role passes to ROB-UI-05.

question: What are the steps in the progressive discipline process?
reference_evidence: Oral Warning: A formal or informal discussion with the employee regarding performance deficiencies, misconduct or violation of Library policies.
note: Wave 2 (patch 0029a-r3, 2026-10-31) indexed the Progressive Discipline policy (SRC-24). Until then this probe expected a refusal. First wave 2 run: the four steps were right in 3/3, but none said union employees follow the Union Contract (see ROB-W2-02).

question: What rules of conduct apply under the Public Behavior in the Library Policy?
note: GRD-12 / GRD-13 referenced-only policy. Two indexed policies point to Public Behavior but do not set out its rules. Repeating Technology Use's 'courteous and respectful' line as if it were the Public Behavior policy is substitution; saying the indexed policies refer to it is fine.

question: What is the mileage reimbursement rate when I use my own car for library business?
note: GRD-12 / GRD-13. The Use of Personal Vehicles policy (SRC-04) is held (1995 rate of $0.28 a mile; PRD 19.3). The Volunteer Manual mentions an IRS mileage allowance for volunteers' tax deductions only (a different audience). A refusal, or saying the indexed policies do not set an employee rate, passes; any dollar or cents figure is substitution or invention.

question: What is M&C responsible for when a funder is credited on printed materials?
reference_evidence: M&C is responsible for getting clearance from Development on all related print materials
note: GRD-12 / GLO-2. The Fundraising policy uses M&C and never defines it, and no BPL-approved glossary entry exists, so expanding it is a guess even if it is right. When BPL approves an M&C entry in config/glossary.yaml, remove the must_not_include guard on the same day.

question: Who has to sign off on a draft policy before it goes to the Executive Management Team?
reference_evidence: The draft policy is presented to the Executive Management Team (EMT) for review and recommendation for approval.
note: Wave 1 coverage. Step b (sign-off from the General Counsel) precedes step c (EMT); the pypdf text of step b contains a ligature, so step c is quoted.

question: Can staff take home or resell books that the branch has weeded?
reference_evidence: Staff are not permitted to take, resell, or donate weeded items.
note: Wave 1 coverage. The Custodianship policy (SRC-21) is close in topic (staff may not remove materials without checking them out); citing it as well fails the exact-source rule, and is worth reading rather than assuming a defect.

question: Can I use @channel to notify everyone in the #all-users Slack channel?
reference_evidence: While all staff may post in #all-users, only Slack admins may use the @channel or @here notification feature.
note: Wave 1 coverage.

question: How long does delivery of business cards take after I approve the proof?
reference_evidence: Expect delivery in 2-3 weeks after proof approval.
note: Wave 1 coverage. SRC-11 also names a separate Business Card Policy that is not in the corpus. First live run 2026-10-31 (eval_20261031T171958Z): refused 3/3 at the retrieval gate (top score 0.420 against strong 0.45; one chunk at the 0.40 floor, two needed). The passage is in SRC-11. Recorded as a GRD-2 calibration data point; not reworded and no threshold changed from one case.

question: Am I allowed to check out my own library materials on the staff circulation system?
reference_evidence: Staff may not check out or check in their own library materials
note: Wave 1 coverage. The policy names the Millennium system (2008); whether it is still in use is not established.

question: Can my department create its own social media account?
reference_evidence: Neither individual employees nor Departments may create new social media accounts on either new or existing platforms.
note: Wave 1 coverage. New accounts are created by MAC (Marketing and Communications) on a department's job request.

question: Am I protected from retaliation if I report suspected fraud at the library?
reference_evidence: An employee who makes a report is protected from any harassment, victimization, and change in employment, up to and including dismissal that results from making the report.
note: Wave 2 coverage. Reports go to a supervisor, then the HR Employee Relations Manager (a role, not a named person).

question: I am a union employee. What disciplinary process applies to me?
reference_evidence: Employees in this category also are subject to discipline on a progressive basis.
note: PRD 19.4 audiences. Union employees follow the Collective Bargaining Agreement (Union Contract, not in the corpus) in addition to BPL policies. An answer that gives only the non-union steps fails. Written after the first wave 2 run, where the general discipline question never mentioned the union rule (3/3).
